summary: The design fits the existing SPA and Bearer-token seams, but several operational and ceremony-state contracts need to be made explicit. The highest risks are dependency resolution, generic 401 handling, username-first versus conditional challenges, and duplicated inline JavaScript.

suggestions.title: Pin and lock the passkey-capable navigator-auth version
suggestions.rationale: The workspace requires navigator-auth >=0.28.3, while uv.lock resolves 0.28.7 and contains no webauthn package entry. PasskeyAuth lazily imports webauthn and raises ConfigError when the optional extra is absent; add a server passkey extra with a >=0.28.9 floor, include it in the aggregate extra if intended, regenerate uv.lock, and test a clean install.

suggestions.title: Separate public passkey calls from the generic 401 interceptor
suggestions.rationale: apiClient converts every 401 into AuthStore.handle401(), while PasskeyAuth uses 401 for origin rejection, expired challenges, invalid assertions, and missing sessions. Login.svelte already bypasses apiClient for unauthenticated discovery because the interceptor corrupts ?next= redirects. Use a public transport for login/options and passkey login, and a controlled Bearer transport for ceremonies so expected passkey errors remain inline without silently logging the user out.

suggestions.title: Specify the challenge state machine for conditional and username-first login
suggestions.rationale: The backend only populates allowCredentials and expected_user_id when login/options receives a username. Therefore the initial empty username challenge cannot provide true username-first semantics after the user types a name. Cache the one usernameless challenge for conditional UI, abort it on explicit click, fetch a username-scoped challenge when needed, and abort pending work on component teardown or navigation.

suggestions.title: Model the actual endpoint statuses and payloads explicitly
suggestions.rationale: The backend returns login options as challenge_id plus publicKey, registration verification as 201 with an id, credentials as a bare array, rename success as JSON, and delete success as 204. Credential IDs are base64url path segments and labels are trimmed and constrained to 1–128 characters. The API module should encode IDs, avoid parsing a 204 body, and preserve {reason} errors rather than treating all endpoints as one generic CRUD envelope.

suggestions.title: Make cross-RP management and last-login protection visible
suggestions.rationale: GET credentials lists the user’s credentials across all relying parties and returns only rp_id; deletion can return 409 when it would remove the last login method. The security UI should display the RP identifier, avoid assuming every credential belongs to the current origin, treat 409 as an authoritative refusal, and refresh after mutations instead of optimistically removing records.

suggestions.title: Exclude PasskeyAuth from generic provider rendering
suggestions.rationale: ProviderButtons currently excludes only BasicAuth. If PasskeySignIn is added separately, PasskeyAuth will otherwise remain as a disabled non-external provider and produce a duplicate, misleading control. Filter by the case-insensitive X-Auth-Method header and add a discovery test asserting the passkey method is absent from ProviderButtons while the dedicated component is present.

suggestions.title: Use separate explicit-support and conditional-support capability checks
suggestions.rationale: PublicKeyCredential availability is sufficient to offer explicit sign-in, but conditional mediation and the native JSON parsing helpers are optional. Keep the hand-written conversion fallback independent from conditional-UI detection; jsdom has neither credentials nor realistic WebAuthn APIs, so tests must cover native, fallback, unsupported-conditional, AbortError, and NotAllowedError paths.

suggestions.title: Create a contract test for the duplicated inline ceremony
suggestions.rationale: The inline page is a separate HTML/JavaScript implementation and the route is registered independently by the orchestrator. There is no current test covering _ADMIN_LOGIN_HTML. Add a smoke/contract test for the passkey control, username autocomplete, public options probe, abort behavior, uniform failure rendering, token/session persistence, and redirect behavior; otherwise the SPA and inline page will drift silently.

suggestions.title: Test the new route across both SPA and aiohttp contracts
suggestions.rationale: config.appSections is the router’s first-segment whitelist, while serving.py owns the actual shell routes and auth exclusions. Existing serving tests hard-code the current sections. Add /account and /account/security to UI route/guard tests and Python deep-link/exclusion tests so a hard reload cannot regress into a 404 or auth middleware block.

suggestions.title: Verify exact Origin behavior through the Vite proxy
suggestions.rationale: Production API URLs are relative, while Vite proxies /api to localhost:5000 with changeOrigin enabled. Passkey RP resolution uses an exact normalized Origin and rejects unlisted origins. A mocked unit test cannot prove the browser’s Origin survives dev proxying; add a browser/integration check for production same-origin and http://localhost:5173 development, with both documented in configuration examples.

suggestions.title: Factor one session-envelope persistence path
suggestions.rationale: AuthStore.login currently validates data.token, stores the raw token under ai_parrot_token, stores the complete response under ai_parrot_session, and updates in-memory state. Passkey login must use exactly that path so Topbar, 401 handling, formdesigner, and admin.py interoperate; test both methods against the same storage and user-payload contract.

suggestions.title: Document startup and infrastructure prerequisites, not only browser setup
suggestions.rationale: The current operator guide documents BasicAuth but not PasskeyAuth, while navigator-auth refuses an empty PASSKEY_RELYING_PARTIES map and initializes a Redis-backed single-use challenge store. The passkey section should show the exact backend list, JSON RP configuration for production and Vite dev, the optional install extra, Redis compatibility, shared AUTH_SECRET_KEY expectations, and the expected startup failure modes.
